newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline called higher on refinery blast.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline called higher on refinery blast.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline was called higher Tuesday on news of a blast at Citgo Petroleum Corp's 150,00 barrel per day (bpd) refinery in Corpus Christi, Texas.
Crude was seen consolidating Monday's sharp gains although the blockade of the Sullom Voe oil port by Shetland fisherman has delayed the loading schedule for Brent crude.
Gasoline was called 0.25 to 0.50 cent gallon higher while heating oil was called steady to 0.25 cent a gallon lower. Crude was called steady to five cents lower a barrel.

The blast at the Corpus Christi refinery occurred in one of the plant's process units and a fire that followed the blast is under control and will be allowed to burn out, local emergency services officials said.
Neither CITGO nor the officials had an estimate of damage. The cause of the explosion is still under investigation, fire officials said.
Meanwhile, local police reached the blockade at Sullom Voe this morning in an attempt to break up it up.
"The delay has not been for that long," said Victor Yu, vice president of Refco Inc, who said the blockade has so far not a had a material impact on supply.
Meanwhile, fresh fighting in Nigeria's oil-producing Niger delta has forced oil giant Royal Dutch Shell Group to cut Nigerian oil output by more than 10 percent.
But traders were shrugging off the news, noting the region's common operational shutdowns of late.
"There are so many shutdowns there that until we see an actual force majeure, then we will respond," said a New York trader.
Monday, June crude oil closed up 95 cents at $21.38 a barrel, having peaked at $21.55, after gapping up at the open through a key technical resistance level just above $20.50.
June gasoline ended up 1.58 cents at 64.47 cents a gallon while June heating oil settled up 2.13 cents at 56.65 cents.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
